key_insight: Automatic differentiation reveals that aerodynamic information from sparse pressure probes travels through compressible flows in highly non-uniform, localized patterns, so observability is flow-dependent rather than uniform.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to choose informative sensor locations and improve inverse design or parameter identification in compressible aerodynamics.
method: Propagate gradients through the full unsteady flow solution
Define an AD-based observability metric for sparse pressure probes
evidence_signal: Inverse-learning experiments on compressible flow cases show that high observability usually helps parameter recovery, but the most observable probe is not always the best for inference.
watch_item: Observability scores may not directly translate to optimal inference performance, so sensor placement should be validated with full inverse-learning tests.
paper_title: Information Transport and Observability in Compressible Aerodynamics
